# Benoit Busser, PharmD, PhD

## Professor of Biochemistry & Cancer Sciences · Medical Biochemist

**Elemental Pathology · BioLIBS · Metals & Health · Translational Research**

I develop translational approaches at the interface of laboratory medicine, environmental and occupational health, cancer sciences and elemental imaging, with a particular focus on laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) applied to human tissues.

[Research](research.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg}

## Research at a glance

:::: {.grid .home-grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .home-card}
### Elemental Pathology & BioLIBS

Tissue elemental imaging to visualize, localize and quantify endogenous and exogenous elements, particles and elemental signatures in biological specimens.

**Applications:** lung disease, environmental and occupational exposure, cancer and biomaterials.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .home-card}
### Metals & Health

Research on the links between metals, particles, human exposure and disease, from analytical characterization to biological interpretation and clinical translation.

**Approach:** chemistry, pathology, imaging and translational medicine.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .home-card}
### Cancer Sciences

Translational cancer research combining tumor biology, analytical sciences, imaging and theranostic approaches.

**Focus:** clinically meaningful biomarkers and innovative technologies for precision medicine.
:::
::::

## From tissue chemistry to clinical questions

My work aims to connect **what is present in a tissue**, **where it is located**, and **what it may mean for disease, exposure or patient care**. This translational perspective links analytical development with pathology, clinical biochemistry and multidisciplinary medical research.

## Academic & clinical environment

My activities are based at **Université Grenoble Alpes**, **Grenoble Alpes University Hospital (CHU Grenoble Alpes)** and the **Institute for Advanced Biosciences (Inserm U1209 / CNRS UMR 5309 / UGA)**.
